# Live-cell imaging in an incubator {#sec-incubator}

A Lumascope can image inside a cell-culture incubator. Its cables pass
through the incubator's port (@sec-incubator-port). Clean it before it goes
in (@sec-sanitizing), and set up the computer for a long time-lapse
(@sec-windows-timelapse).

## Putting the microscope into a warm, humid incubator {#sec-incubator-in}

A room-temperature microscope placed in a warm, humid incubator gathers
condensation. Do not do this. Instead:

1. Turn on the incubator's internal fan, if it has one.
2. Remove the humidification: turn off an active humidifier, or take out the
   pans of water. Do not leave the door open; it invites contamination.
3. When the incubator is warm and dry, place the microscope on its shelf.
4. Wait 2 to 4 hours for the microscope to reach the incubator's
   temperature.
5. Restore the humidification: turn the humidifier back on, or put the pans
   of water back.

## Taking the microscope out {#sec-incubator-out}

A warm microscope can be taken out of a humid incubator and put on the bench
at any time: it is warmer than the room, so no water condenses on it.

::: {.callout-warning title="Condensation ruins the microscope"}
- Do not move the microscope into and out of the incubator again and again:
  each move puts its optics and electronics through a cycle of condensation
  and evaporation.
- Take the microscope out of the incubator before turning the incubator off.
  An incubator cooling down condenses its moisture onto the microscope.
- Do not turn the microscope off while it is in a humid incubator.
:::
